name: Doodle Rescue 3D
tagline: Sketch it. Build it. Save the puppy.
description: A 3D physics drawing adventure built in Godot 4 and rendered straight in the browser. Drag a finger across the diorama and the glowing pencil leaves a real 3D beam with real collision: plug the round doorway of Biscuit's kennel, a deck for him to cross a ravine, a wall to turn a rolling boulder, or a ramp that drops a toy ball into a basket. The puppy reacts to everything — ears back when the bees get close, a little spin when he is safe — and the results are decided by the simulation that actually ran, not a scripted answer. Four toy worlds hold 20 hand-built levels, each with a stored solution that the shipping physics re-runs before release. In Bee Defence the doorway is a structural puzzle: your doodle fills the round opening, but if it does not bite the wooden frame on both sides the swarm will shove the whole plug in. A measured pen budget on every level, three stars for an efficient rescue, a journey map, cosmetic pens unlocked with stars, and progress that saves locally and syncs to a Little Joy Arcade account.
highlights: Genuine 3D drawing: every stroke becomes a rounded 3D beam with real collision, not a flat line
Bee Defence is structural: fill the round kennel doorway, catch the frame on both sides, or watch the swarm shove your doodle in
Four play styles — Bee Defence, Bridge Build, Danger Dodge and Contraptions — sharing one pencil
Biscuit the puppy: oversized eyes, floppy ears, blinking, breathing, nervous trembles and a victory spin
20 hand-built levels across four toy worlds, each replayed by the shipping physics before release
Three stars for an efficient rescue: the result card shows exactly how much pen you used
Bridge decks sag under Biscuit's weight, and the walker meets the same collision the beams use
Cosmetic pen tin unlocked with stars — a different colour, never different physics
Stars, trophies and your place in the journey save locally and sync through a Little Joy Arcade account
Portrait-first with a full-bleed 3D diorama that also adapts to desktop windows
Reduced-motion and low-quality options for older phones
howToPlay: Drag on the scene with a mouse or finger. A glowing pencil line previews the beam.
Bee levels: scribble across the round doorway. The doodle fills the hole; if it does not catch the wooden frame on both sides, the bees can shove it in.
Let go to build it: the stroke becomes a real 3D structure with real collision.
Press Play. Bees attack, Biscuit crosses, boulders roll, or the ball starts moving.
Keep Biscuit safe for the whole timer, or get him to the flag. Draw again and retry as often as you like.
Use less pen for more stars. The bar shows the 3★ threshold before you press Play.
